title: tenant-aware cache-ecology + microburst fallback profiles
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Motivation: Production workloads show wide variance in tenant access patterns: steady traffic tenants get large effective cache hit rates, while bursty tenants cause cache churn and tail latency spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight "cache ecology" controller that synthesizes per-tenant eviction and residency profiles from recent access histograms and a microburst fallback that temporarily reduces batch size and switches to microbatch-optimized execution paths when burst detection and KV-cache churn would otherwise violate latency SLOs.

What this changes: Adds an inference-side service and control loop that: 1) ingests tenant-level access metrics (prefix length, inter-arrival, hit/miss ratios) and produces a ranked set of eviction policies (LRU-variant, segmented-TTL, weighted-residency) and quantization rollback hints; 2) exposes a profile API used by the scheduler to apply tenant-scoped cache and batching overrides; 3) implements a fast-path microburst detector that toggles a microbatch executor and reduces prefetch aggressiveness for the affected tenant for a short cooldown window. The goal is to reduce cost from repeated cache thrashing while preserving 99.9th percentile latency by gracefully degrading to microbatches rather than dropping requests or causing large KV-cache recomputations.

Design notes: The controller runs in the serving plane with bounded CPU and memory budgets and uses exponentially-weighted histograms with a sliding window to avoid storing per-request traces. Profiles are versioned and lightweight (<=2KB). We intentionally keep the policy space small (4 eviction families x 3 residency levels) to limit combinatorial explosion and make rollout/safety analysis tractable. The microburst guard implements conservative heuristics first and records signals for later ML-based tuning.

Backward compatibility & safety: Default behavior is a no-op unless a tenant has opted into adaptive profiles. All profile changes are annotated with a safety score and a TTL; the scheduler rejects changes below a configurable safety threshold. We included a forced fallback toggle in the Console and a feature flag for private deployments. No model format changes.

Testing & benchmarks: Unit tests cover eviction generator math, profile serialization, and scheduler integration. Integration tests simulate interleaved steady and burst tenants using the perf-lab harness. On internal staging workloads, we observed: - 12% average token cost reduction across mixed workloads - 18% reduction in 99.9th percentile latency on bursty tenants (microburst path engaged) - negligible impact on steady tenants (sub-1% latency delta).

Rollout plan: Start with a small canary (5 tenants) + telemetry visibility (prefetch/miss-rate/latency per-tenant). If stable for 48h, extend to 20% of production traffic using a canary policy and auto-roll back on elevated P99 or miss rate regressions.

Migration steps: Console toggle and API allow opt-in; no mandatory migration. For Private installs, operators can enable the controller via the helm chart values (see docs change).

Related: ENG-2191 (workload telemetry), ENG-2210 (microburst execution paths).
commits: 3 commits: 1) b3f7d2a - initial controller scaffold + histogram ingestion; 2) 9a5c1f8 - eviction profile generator and policy model; 3) e4d2b76 - microburst detector and microbatch executor integration. Each commit includes unit tests and small integration harness updates.
review_comments: Lena Park: Can you explain how profile churn cost is accounted for? Suggest adding a metric for profile churn and an opt-out TTL. (requested change)
Author (Ravi): Added profile_churn_total and churn_ttl configuration, added to controller.go and dashboard. Please re-review.
Diego Alvarez: Microburst detector thresholds look conservative; consider moving to a percentile-of-percentiles approach for noisy tenants. (comment)
Author (Ravi): Agreed. Adjusted detector to use 99th-percentile over the sliding window and added a noisy-tenant suppression flag. Kept default conservative for safety.
Priya Nair: Integration tests flaky on first run due to harness timing; reran CI and added small sleeps in test harness. Approving after CI green. (approved)
CI Bot: initial CI run failed lint on api proto formatting; fixed in second commit. All checks passed on re-run.
ci_log_summary: Lint -> fail (proto formatting) on first run; unit tests -> pass; integration -> intermittent failures (timing) fixed; full pipeline green after second push. Final status: pass.
benchmarks_summary: Staging perf run (mixed steady+bursty synthetic): token cost -12% avg, P99 latency on bursty tenants -18%, memory overhead for controller ~8MB per replica. Microbatch path engaged for ~3.4% of requests in burst scenario.
release_notes: Introduce tenant-adaptive cache policies and microburst fallback executor. Opt-in only; console toggle and helm values available. Improves cost and tail latency for bursty tenants. (non-breaking)
notes_for_ops: For private installs, set values.adaptiveCache.enabled=true and tune values.adaptiveCache.safetyThreshold. Watch dashboards/tenant-cache-ecology and profile_churn_total. If P99 > baseline or miss_rate spikes, toggle feature off and roll back config. Helm chart bump included.
observability_changes: Adds tenant-prefixed metrics: tenant_cache_hits_total, tenant_cache_misses_total, profile_churn_total, microburst_engaged_total, microbatch_latency_p99. Dashboard JSON included in observability/dashboards.
